messages:
pagerduty-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert: high error rate and latency spike on /continuous-batch endpoints in prod (region-us-west). Triggered 3+ times in last 2 mins. Pager: maria (oncall). thread_ts=1768504321

maria (oncall): ack - I'm on it. seeing 95th p95 token latency > 2.5s and a bunch of 502/504s. rolling alerts show queue depth jumping and microbatch sizes skyrocketing.

kevin (eng-runtime): looking at serving metrics now. I can already see KV cache eviction rate spiked and memory pressure climbed on the batch workers ~5m ago. Possibly cache blowup causing thrashing + scheduling jitter.

maria (oncall): customer impact? any particular tenants?

chris (prod-ops): preliminary telemetry: top 3 affected customers are on dedicated capacity and hitting sustained concurrency > 3k rps. A handful of smaller customers see increased latency too. No widespread error page yet but retries are compounding.

paul (customer-success): +1 on customer hits, I've already received slack DMs from a couple of enterprise contacts complaining about timeouts in their ingestion pipelines. We should update them with ETA and mitigation.

kevin (eng-runtime): hypothesis: recent change to batching optimizer (deployed 01:12 UTC) adjusted microbatch growth heuristics too aggressively under high concurrency, leading to microbatch sizes > target which amplifies KV cache pressure and increases queueing. Regression candidate.

maria (oncall): plan: 1) apply emergency microbatch cap to stabilize queues 2) disable prefix K/V caching for susceptible model-group to stop cache growth 3) route heavy tenants to fallback smaller model variant 4) monitor for recovery, then decide rollback if needed. Any objections?

kevin (eng-runtime): agree. I can push microbatch cap and disable caching for model-group=rlf-1 in config. Will do a canary on 10% of workers first.

deploy-bot: Started config rollout job: job_id=cf-roll-1782, target=continuous-batch-workers, strategy=canary(10%), author=kevin.

kevin (eng-runtime): rollout step 1: applying microbatch cap = 8 and cache_enabled=false for model-group=rlf-1 on canary subset. Command used:

```
redctl config set continuous_batch.microbatch_max=8 --selector "model_group=rlf-1" --apply-canary=10
redctl config set continuous_batch.kv_cache.enabled=false --selector "model_group=rlf-1" --apply-canary=10
```

kevin (eng-runtime): logs from canary workers show queue depth dropping ~40% and p95 latency down ~30% within 90s. Memory pressure stabilizing. No immediate increase in tail error rate on canaries.

maria (oncall): good. promote to 50% then global if stable. Also flip routing: move top-affected tenant(s) to fallback smaller variant (rlf-1-small) using routing policy. chris, can you coordinate traffic switch?

chris (prod-ops): on it. routing update command:

```
redctl route set --tenant tenant-acme --model rlf-1-small --weight 100
```

chris (prod-ops): acme moved, telemetry shows acme latency back to baseline. Repeating for two other tenants now.

maria (oncall): status update for statuspage: brief summary + ETA (mitigations in progress, customers partially routed, monitoring). Paul, pls coordinate external comms.

paul (customer-success): drafting message now: "We are investigating increased latency on continuous-batch. We've applied configuration mitigations and are routing affected traffic; customers should see improvement. We'll follow up with root cause and timeline." Will post after you confirm.

tess (sre-lead): suggestion: set temporary alert lower bounds so we don't miss secondary regressions and enable extra sampling for traces on affected routes. Also start a dedicated trace span correlation for KV cache evictions vs request id - we need data for postmortem.

kevin (eng-runtime): enabling extra sampling and eviction counters now. Command:

```
redctl metrics set sampling.trace_rate=0.5 --selector "service=continuous-batch"
redctl metrics set sampling.kv_eviction=true --selector "service=continuous-batch"
```
deploy-bot: Canary succeeded and promoted to 50% -> 100% (cf-roll-1782). Global rollout complete.

maria (oncall): nice work. post-rollout numbers: p95 latency down to near baseline, error rates trending down. queue depth stable. KV cache eviction rate returned to normal.

kevin (eng-runtime): follow-up actions: revert batching optimizer deploy from 01:12 UTC in staging for validation, then if confirmed revert in prod or patch heuristics. I'll open a revert PR immediately and coordinate with CI.

kevin (eng-runtime): PR opened: github.com/redwood/serving/pull/4923 - revert batching-optimizer tweak. tagging tess for review.

maria (oncall): oncall handoff note: documenting timeline and actions in incident tracker. I'll keep this thread open until we're clear for 24h. If we see any recurrence, page SRE.

paul (customer-success): sent initial update to affected customers. They acknowledge and asked for RCA and next steps.

chris (prod-ops): keeping runtime autoscaler paused for a bit to avoid oscillations due to the configuration change. Will re-enable after 1h if stable.

tess (sre-lead): opening incident ticket and assigning postmortem owners: kevin (root cause), maria (mitigation timeline), chris (ops playbook updates), paul (customer comms). Please include relevant metrics: microbatch size distribution, KV cache insert/evict rate, queue depth, per-tenant latency.

maria (oncall): final: system stable, continuing to monitor. If any of you see a regression, call me. Thanks all for quick responses. :thumbsup:
